newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs, pork bellies end limit up on Taiwan news.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs, pork bellies end limit up on Taiwan news.

text.p: News from Taiwan that it was halting exports of pork due to an outbreak of foot and mouth disease in hogs sparked a short covering rally that left CME hog and pork belly futures up their respective limits at the close, traders said.

April through October hog futures ended up the 2.000 cent per lb daily limit with April at 70.275 cents. Other months were up 1.950 to 0.900 cents. March through August pork bellies finished up the 3.000-cent limit with May at 76.300 cents.
Pork complex contracts surged daily limits on talk a halt in the flow of Taiwanese pork to other countries could boost demand for U.S. pork, traders said.
"We were technically oversold (in hog futures) and the trade got hit with the surprise news out of Taiwan," said Don Roose, president of U.S. Commodities Inc.

Taiwan banned exports of pork due to the outbreak and Japan, its biggest customer, and other importers of Taiwan pork are expected to switch to other sources. Japan had been importing about 16,000 tonnes of Taiwan fresh and frozen pork per month -- demand that could be filled by pork producers in the U.S., Canada and Europe, sources said.
The only problem traders see in moving pork quickly to Japan is the current safeguard tariffs Japan has in place.

"This is just all an emotional anticipation right now - the problem is the Japanese have implemented the safeguard measure that won't allow any more shipments of (frozen) pork to the Japanese unless they would change the safeguard measure July 1," said Paul Georgy, president of Allendale Inc.
Taiwan also exports to South Korea which is a consumer of pork bellies -- a factor that was particularly supportive to pork belly futures, traders said.
A strong technical reversal also provided strength to both pork pits. The reversal put an island bottom on the charts in both hog and belly futures, chartists said.

Options, as well as the limit up closes, point to further gains Friday. April hog options closed synthetically at 70.700 cents per lb and June at 78.500 while synthetic May bellies closed at 77.500 and July at 77.300. There was active April hog call buying at the close, pit sources said.
Unfilled buy orders were nearly 200 cars in April and 300 in June hogs and over 200 in May bellies, pit sources added.

Estimates on Friday's U.S. Cold Storage report ranged from 41.2 million to 43.0 million lbs on hand March 1. That would be up from 38.04 million on hand the previous month but below 46.38 million on hand March 1, 1996.
